newsitem.title: USA: House ends attack on USDA conservation officials.
newsitem.headline: House ends attack on USDA conservation officials.

text.p: The U.S. House, on a voice vote, ended an attack on two Agriculture Department officials who superintended the enrollment of 16 million acres into the Conservation Reserve this spring.
Members acted on the same day Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman was in Washington state on a fence-mending trip.

Representative George Nethercutt, R-Wash., persuaded the Appropriations Committee a couple of weeks ago to refuse to pay the salaries of the deputy and assistant deputy administrator of the Farm Service Agency. He was piqued because only 172,013 acres were accepted in his state, out of 818,378 acres offered.
"We expect...to have fair treatment of all states of the country," Nethercutt said shortly before the House voted to restore funding.
He said he was assured by Glickman that Washington state would be treated even-handedly when a new Conservation Reserve sign-up was held later this year.
